# Left-Invariant Forms and Structure Equations on the Heisenberg Group $H_3$

## 1. The Heisenberg Group and Its Lie Algebra

The Heisenberg group $H_3 \subset \mathrm{GL}(3,\mathbb{R})$ consists of all upper-triangular matrices with unit diagonal:

$$g = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & x & z \\ 0 & 1 & y \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad x, y, z \in \mathbb{R}.$$

A general element of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{h}_3$ is

$$\begin{pmatrix} 0 & a & c \\ 0 & 0 & b \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix},$$

with basis

$$X = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix},\quad Y = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix},\quad Z = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}.$$

**Bracket computation.**

$$XY = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} = Z, \qquad YX = 0,$$

so $[X,Y] = Z$. Since $Z$ is central, $[X,Z] = [Y,Z] = 0$. The only nonzero structure constant is $c^3_{12} = 1$.

## 2. Left Translation and the Maurer–Cartan Form

**Left translation.** For $g_0 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & x_0 & z_0 \\ 0 & 1 & y_0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$,

$$g_0\, g = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & x_0 + x & z_0 + z + x_0\, y \\ 0 & 1 & y_0 + y \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}.$$

In coordinates this is the map

$$(x, y, z) \;\longmapsto\; \bigl(x_0 + x,\; y_0 + y,\; z_0 + z + x_0\, y\bigr).$$

**Maurer–Cartan form.** We compute $\omega = g^{-1}\, dg$. First

$$g^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -x & xy - z \\ 0 & 1 & -y \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad dg = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & dx & dz \\ 0 & 0 & dy \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}.$$

Then

$$\omega = g^{-1}\, dg = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -x & xy - z \\ 0 & 1 & -y \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} 0 & dx & dz \\ 0 & 0 & dy \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & dx & dz - x\, dy \\ 0 & 0 & dy \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}.$$

Expanding $\omega = \omega^1 X + \omega^2 Y + \omega^3 Z$ (matching the $(1,2)$, $(2,3)$, $(1,3)$ entries) gives the **left-invariant 1-forms**:

$$\boxed{\;\omega^1 = dx, \qquad \omega^2 = dy, \qquad \omega^3 = dz - x\, dy.\;}$$

**Verification of left-invariance.** Under left translation by $g_0$:

- $dx \mapsto d(x_0 + x) = dx$. ✓
- $dy \mapsto d(y_0 + y) = dy$. ✓
- $dz - x\,dy \mapsto d(z_0 + z + x_0 y) - (x_0 + x)\,d(y_0 + y) = (dz + x_0\,dy) - (x_0\,dy + x\,dy) = dz - x\,dy$. ✓

All three forms are invariant, as expected since $\omega = g^{-1}dg$ is by construction left-invariant.

## 3. Structure Equations (Maurer–Cartan)

The Maurer–Cartan structure equations are $d\omega^i = -\sum_{j<k} c^i_{jk}\, \omega^j \wedge \omega^k$. Computing the exterior derivatives:

$$d\omega^1 = d(dx) = 0,$$

$$d\omega^2 = d(dy) = 0,$$

$$d\omega^3 = d(dz - x\,dy) = \underbrace{d(dz)}_{0} - d(x\,dy) = -dx \wedge dy - \underbrace{x\,d(dy)}_{0} = -\omega^1 \wedge \omega^2.$$

Therefore the **structure equations** are:

$$\boxed{\;d\omega^1 = 0, \qquad d\omega^2 = 0, \qquad d\omega^3 = -\,\omega^1 \wedge \omega^2.\;}$$

**Consistency check.** The coefficient of $\omega^1 \wedge \omega^2$ in $d\omega^3$ is $-c^3_{12} = -1$, i.e. $c^3_{12} = 1$, which agrees with $[X, Y] = Z$ computed in §1. The vanishing of $d\omega^1$ and $d\omega^2$ agrees with $[X,Z]=[Y,Z]=0$. The Maurer–Cartan equations are satisfied, confirming the integrability (flatness) of the Maurer–Cartan form on $H_3$.

## 4. Summary

The Heisenberg group $H_3$ with global coordinates $(x, y, z)$ admits the coframe of left-invariant 1-forms

$$\omega^1 = dx, \qquad \omega^2 = dy, \qquad \omega^3 = dz - x\,dy,$$

dual to the Lie algebra basis $\{X, Y, Z\}$ with $[X,Y]=Z$ and $Z$ central. The Maurer–Cartan structure equations are

$$d\omega^1 = 0, \qquad d\omega^2 = 0, \qquad d\omega^3 = -\omega^1 \wedge \omega^2,$$

reflecting the single nonzero bracket $[X,Y]=Z$ of the Heisenberg algebra.

### PROOF COMPLETE
